text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A new international airport is to be built on a man-made island to be reclaimed off the Kuala Muda coast, about 140 km from Alor Star in northern Kedah state.

-- The Sibu Sessions Court in east Malaysia's Sarawak state made what lawyers claimed to be a record when it sat for seven hours to hear a total of 2,372 charges against a businessman and his wife for alleged forgery involving cheques worth 9.3 million ringgit.

-- As the Coxsackie B Virus claimed its 23rd victim on Wednesday, the Cabinet has decided that schools in Sarawak should not be closed as none of the fatalities so far were above the age of four and a half years.

-- The chief ministers of central Selangor state and southern Johor state have warned their state executive councillors to disassociate themselves from business dealings both directly or through proxies.
-- Hospitals nationwide have been directed to comply with three sets of protocol in identifying and treating Coxsackie virus B victims, Health Minister chua Jui Meng said.
-- The government has identified some companies which continue to source from overseas products that are readily available locally.
-- The institution of civil remedies for securities law violations will allow shareholders to sue companies over corporate crimes such as insider trading or making misleading statements.
-- House prices can come down by 10 percent to 15 percent if red tape in getting approvals from government departments is minimised, according to the Housing Developers Association.
